events.title: Henry I Crowned King of England
events.description: Henry I was crowned at Westminster Abbey just days after the sudden death of his brother, King William II. He moved quickly to secure the throne while his eldest brother, Robert Curthose, was still returning from the First Crusade.
events.significance: Henry's swift coronation began a 35-year reign that reshaped English law and government. He also issued the Charter of Liberties, an early forerunner of later limits on royal power.

events.title: England Claims Its First Colony in North America
events.description: Sir Humphrey Gilbert landed at St. John's harbour in Newfoundland. He claimed the territory for Queen Elizabeth I, establishing England's first overseas colony in North America.
events.significance: The claim set a precedent for English expansion across the Atlantic. It paved the way for later settlements such as Jamestown and Plymouth.

events.title: The Mayflower Sets Sail from Southampton
events.description: The Mayflower left Southampton on its first attempt to cross the Atlantic. The voyage was later interrupted by leaks in its companion ship, the Speedwell, and the Mayflower finally departed from Plymouth the following month.
events.significance: The Mayflower's journey became a founding story of English settlement in New England and of American national identity.

events.title: Marilyn Monroe Found Dead
events.description: The actress and model Marilyn Monroe was found dead of a barbiturate overdose at her home in Brentwood, Los Angeles. She was 36 years old.
events.significance: Her death shocked the world and cemented her status as an enduring icon of Hollywood and 20th-century popular culture.

events.title: Oak Creek Sikh Temple Shooting
events.description: A white supremacist gunman opened fire at a Sikh temple in Oak Creek, Wisconsin. He killed six people and wounded four others.
events.significance: The attack drew national attention to hate-motivated violence against religious minorities. It also led to stronger efforts to track and counter domestic extremism.
